clue.text: Fashion right now in Sussex resort

indicators.note: to fashion something is to shape it anew, so the two words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark on what is currently stylish in a south-coast seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' looks like a noun naming what is trendy, but it is a verb telling you to reshape RIGHTNOW; 'in' is a link. WORTHING is a seaside town in West Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Worthing is a seaside town on the West Sussex coast, an example of an English holiday resort.

clue.text: Arms for protection of those behind screen?

definitions.text: Arms for protection of those behind screen?

parts.words: Arms for protection of those behind screen?
parts.note: reads as weapons for a bodyguard, but the arms are the moving blades that clear a car windscreen so the driver behind it can see

explanation.walkthrough: The 'screen' is a windscreen and the 'arms' are the blades that sweep it.
explanation.definitionFit: Windscreen blades on swinging arms keep the glass clear for the driver.

indicators.note: says the work goes inside the word for circus

parts.note: the ring is the arena of a circus
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Doing a circus act that involves binding someone with cord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts OP inside RING.
explanation.definitionFit: Securing something with cord or a lasso is tying it up.

parts.note: a hero is a victor or champion

explanation.surface: Someone called Victor North shows off a bird in the marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victor North' reads as a person's name; 'showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged grey bird that stands in shallow water to fish is a wader.

clue.text: Great bat, Len, caught out sadly

indicators.note: sadly signals that the letters before it come out in a sorry jumble

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A batsman called Len, a great player, is sadly out caught.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface hides a flying mammal: 'sadly' rearranges LEN, C and OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: The noctule is a large European bat, also called the great bat.

clue.text: Press long to lead with a scoop

indicators.note: says the word for press comes first, leading the letter for long

parts.note: to press forward is to shove

explanation.surface: An instruction to push hard and for a long time, starting with a scoop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lead with' puts SHOVE in front of L; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A spade-like tool for lifting loose material is a scoop.

parts.note: suggests electrical therapy, but a shock here is a thick mass of hair, and the treatment is grooming it

explanation.walkthrough: A 'shock' of hair is a thick bushy mop.
explanation.definitionFit: A brush used for grooming tidies a mop of hair.

clue.text: The very words of eccentric ambivert

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A quotation from someone both introvert and extrovert, an odd character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges AMBIVERT; 'of' is a link. An ambivert has both introvert and extrovert traits.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbatim means word for word, quoting exactly what was said.

clue.text: Tiller girls in the second row?

definitions.text: Tiller girls in the second row?

parts.words: Tiller girls in the second row?
parts.note: the Tiller Girls were a high-kicking dance troupe, but here tillers are women farming the soil, in the Second World War

explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Land Army sent women to work on farms in the Second World War; 'row' is both a chorus line and a conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: Women recruited to farm work during the wars formed a civilian agricultural corps.

clue.text: Briers may stand out in this production

definitions.text: Briers may stand out in this production

parts.words: Briers may stand out in this production
parts.note: briers are tobacco pipes made of brier root, and the phrase reads as a theatre review where the actor Richard Briers stands out; the item meant is a stand that holds smokers' pipes upright

explanation.surface: A theatre review saying the actor Richard Briers shines in this show.
explanation.walkthrough: A brier is a pipe made from the root of the white heath; a rack displays such pipes standing out from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand for storing tobacco pipes holds briers upright on display.

clue.text: Fruit from Channel Islands, badly torn

indicators.note: badly torn means the letters of torn are messed up and reordered

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit imported from Jersey or Guernsey arrives damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges TORN to TRON, which follows CI.
explanation.definitionFit: A citron is a large lemon-like citrus fruit grown for its thick peel.
A present is something given, and a natural talent is also called a flair.

indicators.note: being in a storm suggests the letters are tossed about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Flowers unfurling their petals as a gale blows through the meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is UNCURL IN A; the second 'in a', in 'in a storm', is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranunculus is the botanical genus of buttercups, and this is its Latin plural.

clue.text: Portuguese scholar in an attire for retirement

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the words before are read in reverse order

parts.note: an gives the article A
garb is clothing or attire

explanation.surface: A Portuguese academic putting on a gown when retiring from teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for retirement' turns A GARB round to BRAGA; 'in' is a link. Teófilo Braga was a Portuguese scholar, writer and president.
explanation.definitionFit: Teófilo Braga was a nineteenth-century Portuguese man of letters and historian of literature.

parts.note: the traditional song begins 'Speed, bonnie boat' and tells of Bonnie Prince Charlie carried over the sea to a Hebridean island

explanation.walkthrough: The Skye Boat Song tells how Flora MacDonald carried Bonnie Prince Charlie, the royal fugitive, over the sea to the island; 'speedboat' splits into its opening words 'Speed, bonnie boat'.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is the Inner Hebridean island where the Jacobite prince fled by boat in 1746.

clue.text: Leather finally chosen for backing novel

parts.note: kid is soft leather made from goatskin
in racing a nap is the tipster's best bet, so a horse napped is one picked to be backed

explanation.surface: A leather item eventually picked out to be used as backing material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' is a link meaning 'and then'. Kidnapped is Robert Louis Stevenson's novel of 1886.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenson's adventure story of David Balfour is a well-known work of fiction.

parts.note: going places and doing them, as in 'doing Rome', describes the holiday trade of visiting sights

explanation.walkthrough: To 'do' a city is to see its sights, so travelling there and doing it is the sightseeing industry.
explanation.definitionFit: Travel for pleasure, visiting places and seeing the sights, is the activity of holidaymakers.

parts.note: a bar is a pub
codes are sets of rules

explanation.surface: Looking over the rule book of a public house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Striped labels read by a laser at the checkout are patterns that get scanned.

clue.text: Where, in France, a river meanders for so long

indicators.note: a river that meanders winds about, so these letters wander into a new order

parts.note: the French for where is où

explanation.surface: A French river winding its way along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meanders' rearranges OU and A RIVER together; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The French farewell means goodbye until we meet again, like the casual English parting phrase.

indicators.note: doing something freshly is doing it anew, so the letters of launder are made over

explanation.surface: Washing some articles of clothing again at a home in the south of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freshly' rearranges LAUNDER; 'items' is a link standing for the place sought. ARUNDEL is a castle town in West Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Arundel is a market town with a famous castle in the West Sussex district of Arun.
Written records of a voyage, and logarithm tables used to simplify calculation.

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Chest pain felt as a heavy sensation around the heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The four letters straddle 'cardiAC HEaviness'; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull continuous pain is an ache.

indicators.note: says the gallery comes after the champion

parts.note: an ace is a champion or expert
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: An art gallery comes next after a top performer cuts a disc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts TATE after ACE; 'making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An acetate is a disc cut for a trial pressing of a recording.

clue.text: Tuba, we hear, making big sum at job-centre

parts.note: a pot is a large sum of money

indicators.note: the centre of the word job is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A tuba player strikes it rich at the employment office.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a homophone: 'Tuba, we hear' sounds like tuber, and a potato is a tuber. 'centre' takes O from job; 'making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A starchy underground stem eaten as a vegetable is the classic tuber.
People or machines that add up figures, and venomous snakes of the viper family.

clue.text: Chosen leaders knocking back beer and lobster claw

indicators.note: the leading letters of the word chosen, here the opening pair
knocking back means the word for beer is turned round, punning on drinking it down

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Elected chiefs downing pints while eating seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' takes CH from Chosen; 'knocking back' turns ALE into ELA; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A chela is the pincer of a crustacean such as a crab or lobster.

explanation.surface: A tough tree growing in the ancient Hampshire woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hardy's novel is 'Under the Greenwood Tree'; a greenwood is also a forest in fresh leaf. The New Forest is an ancient woodland in Hampshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardy's novel title names a tree of the leafy woods, and a wood in full new leaf is the other sense.

parts.note: arks are boats or vessels

explanation.surface: Fruit from Australia packed in boats in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peaches' is a verb, informs on; in Australian slang to nark is also to annoy. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To nark is slang for informing to the police, as is to peach.

indicators.note: the word for dreary goes round the other letters

parts.note: dry means dull or dreary
O is a ring by its shape
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A listless piece of jewellery-making done in a dull circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts DRY around O and OP; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something drooping and lacking energy is languid.

clue.text: Blonde, feisty, a reasonable target for criticism

parts.note: fair hair is blonde
game means plucky or feisty

explanation.surface: A spirited blonde woman finds herself the butt of criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: A legitimate object of attack or ridicule is someone it is acceptable to criticise.

clue.text: One step of a street journey

parts.note: a ride is a journey

explanation.surface: A single pace taken along the road at the start of a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A long pace in walking counts as a single step.

explanation.surface: Retirement income drawn from owning French holiday homes.
explanation.walkthrough: In France a pension is a boarding house or small hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular retirement payments are income, and French boarding houses are lodging properties.
